It's March now, and my wheat is starting to turn green after winter. I've been farming this land since I was 21 — 15 years now — so I know every plot. My farm is 19 mu total. I keep about 12 mu for wheat and maize back-to-back, and the other 7 mu I plant cotton. That's what works for my family. My husband works at a factory in the county town and sends money home, so I'm the one managing the farm day-to-day. My parents live with us and help when their legs allow, and my two kids are in school, so they only help on weekends.

**For the wheat** — I planted it last October, put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu then as base. Now it's green-up time. Last year I topdressed with about 25 kg of urea per mu and got around 450 kg/mu. My neighbor Auntie Li told me she cut back to 15 kg of urea this spring to save money, but her wheat looks yellow and thin already. I'm not taking that risk — I'd rather waste a little money on fertilizer than lose half my yield. I'll put down about 20 kg of urea per mu when the wheat turns green, and if it still looks hungry at jointing, I'll add another 5 kg. I irrigate three times: once now in spring, once at jointing, and once when the grains are filling. Pumping water costs about 20 yuan each time per mu, but without water there's no yield. I spray twice for bugs and fungus — aphids always come, and the wet spring brings disease.

**For the cotton** — I'll plant it in late April, after I finish the spring wheat work. I need to plow and make ridges first. I use about 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and then topdress with about 15 kg of urea when the plants flower. Cotton is a lot of hand work — planting, thinning, spraying for bollworms, and picking. I spray four or five times for bollworms; they're worse every year. I irrigate twice — once at flowering and once when the bolls are growing. The big cost is picking. My family can't handle 7 mu of cotton alone, so I hire three or four women from the village for about 15 to 20 days in September and October. That costs a lot, but I have no choice.

**For the maize** — I plant in mid-June, right after I cut the wheat. The window is tight, sometimes only five or six days. I hire a combine to harvest the wheat, then I plant the maize immediately. I use hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer in the rows when I plant, and topdress with about 15 kg of urea at the big trumpet stage if the plants look like they need it. Last year I got about 500 kg/mu. I irrigate twice if the rain is decent — once after planting and once when it's tasseling. September and October are always crazy — picking cotton, harvesting maize, and trying to plant wheat all at once. That's why I need the hired help.

Money is tight with eight people in the house, even with my husband's factory wages. I buy mid-grade seed — not the cheapest, not the most expensive. I watch every yuan, but I won't cut fertilizer so much that I risk the yield. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, so I play it safe.
